questions.question: What does smoothly downshifting on a motorcycle do?

options.text: It lets the engine help slow the motorcycle.
You should not do it around other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: It lets the engine help slow the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Engine braking from downshifting can help motorcyclists slow down. If you use engine braking, also use your brake lights so other drivers know you are slowing down.

questions.question: What material are motorcycle riding gloves usually made from?
questions.explanation: Motorcycle riding gloves are usually made of leather. They improve your grip and protect your hands and fingers.

questions.question: When should a rider use their mirrors?
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors when slowing down, stopping, at intersections, changing lanes, and turning.

questions.question: Which item is NOT protective clothing for a motorcycle rider?
questions.explanation: Wear protective clothing that includes a jacket, sturdy pants, boots that support your ankles, and gloves. A stocking cap is not proper protective gear for riding.

questions.question: Why is riding next to a car dangerous?

options.text: You could be in the driver's blind spot.
It is only a problem on wet roads.
It makes driving easier for the other driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: You could be in the driver's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding beside another vehicle is dangerous because the driver may not see you in their blind spot. The vehicle also blocks your escape route.

questions.question: Which surface is slippery and hard to control a motorcycle on?
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lines, and metal covers are slippery. Ride carefully on these surfaces.

questions.question: What best reduces head and neck injuries?
questions.explanation: A good helmet greatly reduces head and neck injuries. A helmet is your best protection in an accident.

questions.question: How can you be more visible when riding during the day?
questions.explanation: Most crashes happen during the day. Always wear bright-colored clothing when riding, even in daylight.

questions.question: What should motorcycle riding clothing cover?

options.text: Both your arms and legs completely
Your arms completely, but not your legs
Your legs completely, but not your arms
Whatever is most comfortable, regardless of safety

questions.correctAnswerText: Both your arms and legs completely
questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs completely to stay protected while riding.

questions.question: What should you consider when choosing a lane position?

options.text: Whether other drivers can see you
How many cars are ahead of you
Which position lets you pass the most vehicles

questions.correctAnswerText: Whether other drivers can see you
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position where other drivers can see you clearly and where you have enough space to maneuver safely.

questions.question: Regular maintenance on your motorcycle helps because:

options.text: The motorcycle will run well for a long time.
Maintenance checks take a lot of time.
Maintenance checks can prevent parking tickets.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle will run well for a long time.
questions.explanation: A well-maintained motorcycle will continue to run like new. Regular maintenance and inspections keep your motorcycle in good condition.

questions.question: If your shoes have laces, you should:
questions.explanation: Tuck shoelaces in securely while riding. Loose laces can catch on the motorcycle and cause problems.

questions.question: Motorcycles:

options.text: Do not have blind spots because they are small.
Have small blind spots that are not a concern.
Have blind spots you should check regularly.
Are too small to have blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have blind spots you should check regularly.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any vehicle. Turn your head to check blind spots before changing lanes. Make head checks part of your regular scanning routine.

questions.question: When choosing footwear for riding, select:

options.text: Shoes with long laces you cannot tuck in.

questions.explanation: Wear boots or shoes that are sturdy and cover your ankles for support. Heels should be short so they don't catch on surfaces. Laces should be tucked in so they don't catch on motorcycle parts.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to hazards ahead.

questions.question: How do you control the accelerator?
questions.explanation: The accelerator is on the right handlegrip and is controlled with your right hand.

questions.question: To check tire pressure, you should:

options.text: Look at the tire to estimate pressure.
Squeeze the tire with your hand.
Compare the tire height to another tire.

questions.explanation: Use a tire gauge to check tire pressure before every ride. An under-inflated tire may look okay, so visual checks are not reliable.

questions.question: Where is the throttle located?
questions.explanation: The throttle is on the right handlegrip. Know where all controls are located before riding.

questions.question: A motorcycle needs:

options.text: Checks performed only by a mechanic.

questions.explanation: Small problems on a motorcycle are more serious than on a car. Check your motorcycle thoroughly before every ride.

questions.question: Low-speed crashes:

options.text: Happen frequently, so do not worry about them.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen at speeds below 30 miles per hour. Even low-speed crashes can be fatal.

questions.question: Riding at night:

options.text: Is safer when you wear reflective clothing.
Is not safe because other drivers cannot see your turn signals.
Should only be done in the city.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is safer when you wear reflective clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear reflective clothing when riding at night. This makes you more visible to other drivers on the road.

questions.question: When riding, a cushion of space around your motorcycle helps you to:

options.text: Have time to react to hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have time to react to hazards.
questions.explanation: Keep space around your motorcycle at all times. This gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake. You need this space to maneuver safely.

questions.question: For motorcycle safety, you should:

options.text: Assume everything on your motorcycle will work properly.
Check your motorcycle before every ride.
Check your motorcycle once a month.
Check your motorcycle twice a week.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your motorcycle before every ride.
questions.explanation: Small mechanical problems are more dangerous on a motorcycle than on a car. Check your motorcycle carefully before every ride.

questions.question: How can you be more visible at an intersection?

options.text: Swerve within your lane to get attention.

questions.explanation: Use your headlight at an intersection to be more visible. Position your motorcycle in your lane where drivers can see you best. Keep space around your motorcycle so you can take action if needed.

questions.question: You should not ride directly alongside another vehicle because:

options.text: You may be in its blind spot.
It is distracting to have a vehicle next to you.
Other drivers may want to use that lane.
It would be hard to see what is behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in its blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding alongside another vehicle is dangerous because you may be in the driver's blind spot. The driver will not see you. Also, the vehicle can block your escape route if a hazard appears.
